findings.title: split supervisor leaves SIGINT/SIGQUIT at Python defaults
findings.evidence: tests/gates/g2_shell/live_combined_boundary_probe.py split_supervisor only handles SIGTSTP/SIGCONT; after foreground restoration a PTY Ctrl-\ can terminate the observer before finally, producing RETURN:131/WAIT without an explicit unknown latch while a setsid descendant may remain active
findings.required_correction: Keep the split supervisor observable across foreground INT/QUIT, preserve descendant lifetime semantics, and add split-path runtime coverage that distinguishes the signal from numeric exit 131

findings.title: split supervisor cleanup can miss a newly reparented setsid descendant
findings.evidence: cleanup snapshots direct children once and then blocks in waitpid; failure after setsid but before host identity registration can leave an adopted descendant outside both the snapshot and PTY-session cleanup
findings.required_correction: Make failure cleanup bounded and repeated, verify no owned descendants remain, and exercise an injected failure between setsid and host identity registration

scope_limit: The reviewed split_case covers Ctrl-Z, exit 148, parent WAIT, and stale input only; the broader environment/takeover/failure/INT/QUIT matrix still uses shared-PG helpers and is not evidence of completed CW-03 adapter integration.
